ideas.risks: The 1/e constant may fail under finite-support approximation, strict crossing, or transfer to concatenated paths; multi-horizon same-path versions must control intermediate quote rewards when the number of thresholds grows.
ideas.summary: Generalize the two-threshold zero-block lemma to a finite terminal threshold set C. The dual gap should be kappa(C)=sup_lambda E_lambda[C]-sup_a a Pr_lambda(C>a), i.e. welfare minus optimal posted-price revenue. Optimize over lambda and test whether the best zero-block constant is 1/e, achieved approximately by an equal-revenue-type distribution; then lift to universal block concatenations and same-path multi-horizon blocks 0^N,c_1,...,c_m with m=o(N).
ideas.title: Multi-Threshold Block Constant
ideas.why_promising: This is a concrete, separately checkable extension of the accepted 1/4 lemma and may strengthen the lower-bound constant while connecting kappa to known posted-price geometry.

ideas.risks: The prefix-local comparator v_u must be a valid lower bound on the global fixed-action comparator; same-prefix laws can fail for stochastic candidates; rare events and suffix compensation can otherwise create false positives.
ideas.summary: Turn the solver's kappa transfer into a precise lemma. Work on finite grids and finite candidate set U first: condition on a common-prefix event E, assume the learner's prefix action marginals are identical for all u in U, define prefix payoffs phi_{u,t}, and include an explicit outside-surplus cap B_u plus probability weight Pr(E). Prove max_u regret_u >= |I| kappa_I(U)-B, or identify the missing hypotheses.
ideas.title: Kappa Transfer Lemma
ideas.why_promising: It would convert the current prefix-compatibility heuristic into an accepted reusable lower-bound tool, and every assumption can be criticized directly.

ideas.risks: A full characterization may become tautological or computational rather than structural; the best fixed comparator couples all times through one quote, while the learner can vary quotes by time.
ideas.summary: Study the process-aware but horizon-oblivious deterministic-path regime as an offline simultaneous-prefix design problem. Given a known path P_1,P_2,..., characterize when there exists one action sequence a_t whose rewards track V_T^*=sup_a sum_{t<=T} r_t(a) for all T. Use paths 0^N,c_0,c_1 and multi-threshold paths as test cases, and look for a horizon-compatibility modulus that gives both lower and upper bounds.
ideas.title: Known-Path Anytime Characterization
ideas.why_promising: This targets the one quantifier regime where oracle collapse does not apply and where the same-path obstruction is genuinely instance-wise.

ideas.risks: Delayed OCO/bandit results may not map cleanly because market-making feedback is full-information only after public threshold crossings and horizon censoring creates missing zero rewards; tracking all K grid arms may be too expensive without exploiting nesting.
ideas.summary: Replace fixed H truncation with adaptive skipping or tracking-capacity algorithms on the grid problem. Define skipped payoff mass or outstanding weighted feedback, use public prices to close all grid arms below P_s, and attempt a bound in terms of skipped value, total outstanding observations, or capacity C rather than beta(H). Compare with Ryabchenko-Attias-Roy 2025/2026 and delayed-weighted FTRL reductions.
ideas.title: Adaptive Skipping Sufficiency
ideas.why_promising: It could produce a stronger and more usable sufficiency theorem that does not require knowing a tail schedule H_T and aligns with current delayed-learning literature.

ideas.risks: If the rare branch is fully coded, the example may only refute essential-sup tail conditions for process-aware learners; if it is not coded, regret may become nontrivial. All-horizon expected-value bounds need careful summability choices.
ideas.summary: Finish a rare-history construction where positive-probability branches contain arbitrarily long payoff-relevant delays, keeping beta or gamma large through essential sup, while their ex-ante contribution is negligible and/or the branch code makes the optimal quote known. Choose p_n, L_n, and amplitudes so expected regret is o(T) but conditional tails never decay.
ideas.title: Rare-History Tail Failure
ideas.why_promising: This directly tests whether essential-sup tail assumptions are too strong even after payoff weighting, and would sharpen CE-006 into a reusable obstruction.

ideas.risks: Always quoting 1/2 must be checked for every inter-spike horizon, not just spike endpoints; older blocks and strict-crossing nonattainment can add small but annoying terms.
ideas.summary: Formalize the superexponential uniform-spike process: P_{S_n}=U_n with U_n uniform on [0,1], zeros otherwise, S_{n+1}/S_n -> infinity. Prove an anytime simple policy, likely always 1/2, has o(T) regret for all T, while gamma stays bounded away from zero and Delta_{S_n}(H)=Omega(S_n) for H=o(S_n). Determine whether Gamma_T(H) is also linear along spike horizons.
ideas.title: Uniform-Spike Counterexample
ideas.why_promising: It would separate predictable delayed reward mass from learning difficulty more cleanly than the beta-only sparse-vanishing-spike example.

ideas.risks: Approachability controls vector averages under observed vector payoffs, while the market-making deficits involve future-censored rewards and possibly unknown candidate horizons; feedback availability may block a direct algorithm.
ideas.summary: Try to turn prefix compatibility from a lower-bound modulus into an algorithmic sufficient condition. For a finite set of candidate horizons or continuations, define vector deficits against each candidate and ask whether simultaneous Blackwell approachability gives one action rule with small regret to all candidates when kappa-like feasibility gaps vanish or are small.
ideas.title: Simultaneous-Approachability Upper Bound
ideas.why_promising: It offers a possible positive counterpart to the prefix-incompatibility lower bounds and uses new simultaneous approachability literature rather than only delayed-feedback tools.

ideas.risks: This may drift away from the stated pseudo-regret problem; raw beta may still be the wrong statistic even under pathwise regret, so the output may be only a taxonomy.
ideas.summary: Systematically compare pseudo-regret sup_a E[reward(a)] with pathwise regret E[sup_a reward(a)-learner] and with endogenous/adaptive prices. Re-test oracle collapse, stochastic two-continuation mixtures, sparse spikes, and coded delays under each notion to identify whether any tail necessity statement can be salvaged.
ideas.title: Alternative Regret Notions
ideas.why_promising: The original iff may be false mainly because of the pseudo-regret and horizon/law-aware quantifiers; this direction could clarify exactly which nearby formulations remain mathematically meaningful.
